short: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets
title: Binding SnO2 Nanocrystals in Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Sheets as Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Lithium-ion anodes need far more capacity than graphite; SnO2 offers it but pulverises and its Sn aggregates on cycling. Binding small SnO2 nanocrystals inside nitrogen-doped graphene sheets should keep them active, intact and unaggregated.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (DES/route), n6 (PRC/synthesis), n7 (PRC/forming), n8 (PRC/synthesis), n9 (DES/variable_sweep), n10 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: SnO2 nanocrystals are 4-5 nm and the vapour reduction does not coarsen them. Nanocrystals are uniformly confined inside the graphene sheets, with only a few exposed at the outer surface.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), n12 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n13 (STR/phase/identity), n14 (STR/interface), n19 (STR/microstructure/distribution). Premises: JCPDS 41-1445: tetragonal rutile SnO2, P42/mnm, a = 4.738 A, c = 3.187 A; C K-edge intensity at ca. 285 and 288 eV reports carbon bonded to nitrogen and oxygen species

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Graphene carries electrons in and micropores carry Li+ in, while the sheets buffer the volume change and Sn-N bonds stop Sn coarsening. Reversible capacity is 1346 mA h/g after 500 cycles at near-100% Coulombic efficiency.

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The hybrid works as a high-rate, long-life lithium-ion anode

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Binding SnO2 nanocrystals in nitrogen-doped graphene gives a stable, high-capacity, high-rate anode

nodes.title: SEM, F1
nodes.head: SEM at two magnifications: crumpled sheet stacks whose surfaces are smooth, with almost no nanocrystals standing proud
nodes.solves: Nanocrystals are uniformly confined inside the graphene sheets, with only a few exposed at the outer surface
nodes.note: scale bars 10 um (F1a) and 100 nm (F1b), both OCR cues; the high-magnification surface shows only fine texture, no discrete particles
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o2, o3, o4, o5 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM, F1
nodes.head: TEM: dense speckled nanocrystals fill the sheet interior evenly, thinning to bare N-RGO at the sheet edge
nodes.solves: Nanocrystals are uniformly confined inside the graphene sheets, with only a few exposed at the outer surface
nodes.note: the bare graphene margin at the bottom of F1c is arrowed N-RGO, which is what shows the crystals sit inside the sheet
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o1, o3, o4, o5 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM:HRTEM, F1
nodes.head: HRTEM: lattice-fringed crystallites about 4-5 nm across, one marked SnO2 (110), lying against the graphene
nodes.solves: SnO2 nanocrystals are 4-5 nm and the vapour reduction does not coarsen them
nodes.note: sized against the 5 nm scale bar in F1d (OCR cue)
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o1, o2, o4, o5 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM:STEM, F4
nodes.head: STEM before and after 500 cycles: the cycled aggregate is brighter, denser and three times larger with a smooth outer skin
nodes.solves: After 500 cycles Sn is still spread through the carbon with no Sn-rich clusters
nodes.note: scale bars 100 nm (F4a) and 300 nm (F4f), so the two views are not at the same magnification
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and S1 keeps shown support from o1, o2, o3, o4.

nodes.title: XRD, F2
nodes.head: Hybrid and bare-nanocrystal XRD traces both sit on the SnO2 stick pattern, with equally broad peaks and no graphite reflection
nodes.solves: The nanocrystals are polycrystalline tetragonal rutile SnO2 (JCPDS 41-1445)
nodes.note: the (002) graphite reflection expected near 26 deg is not resolved from the SnO2 (110) peak
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o1, o2, o3, o4 after removal.

nodes.title: XAS:XANES, F2
nodes.head: C K-edge traces coincide exactly at the 285.4 eV peak; the hybrid is higher only above ~288 eV, clearly so at 292 eV
nodes.solves: Interfacial Sn-N and Sn-O-C bonds tie the nanocrystals to the doped graphene
nodes.note: the text claims an obvious increase at ca. 285 eV; in F2f the two curves are indistinguishable there
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o1, o2, o3, o4 after removal.

nodes.title: ECHEM:galvanostatic, F3
nodes.head: First discharge reaches ~1865 mA h/g but first charge returns only ~1200, a first-cycle efficiency near 64%. Capacity drops from ~1850 to ~1000 mA h/g by cycle 20, then climbs steadily to ~1350 at cycle 500; efficiency sits at ~100%
nodes.solves: Reversible capacity is 1346 mA h/g after 500 cycles at near-100% Coulombic efficiency
nodes.note: read off the F3b capacity axis; cycles 2 and 3 nearly overlap at ~1200 mA h/g read from F3c; the text quotes 1346 mA h/g after 500 cycles, consistent with the panel

use: The TEM image (Figure 1c) reveals that uniform nanocrystals are homogeneously distributed in the graphene sheets.

The ring-like mode in the selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (inset of Figure 1c) confirms the presence of polycrystalline $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}$ , which can be identified as a tetragonal rutile-like $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}$ (JCPDS No. 41–1445, space group $P4_{2}/m n m$ $a_{0}=b_{0}=4.738\mathrm{~\AA~}$ , $c_{0}=3.187\mathrm{~\AA|}$ by X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Figure 2b).[45,46] Also, the HRTEM image (Figure 1d) displays $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}$ nanocrystals bound in graphene sheets with sizes of $4{-}5~\mathrm{nm}$ , indicating that the size of the $\mathrm{SnO}_{2}$ nanocrystals does not change during the in situ hydrazine monohydrate vapor reduction process.
